page: Microsoft Azure FX96mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor. It features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The system is provisioned with 1832.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 19.08 GB of memory per core, and includes 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier capabilities across memory and database operations. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 103,610.4 and a database operations score of 37,422.58, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly optimized, with read-only small block cached transfers reaching 7,620.93 GB/sec and large block uncached writes at 188.83 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is also in the top tier at 609.06 GB/sec. For transactional workloads, the instance processed 130.32 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 145.38 GB/sec.

Given its high resource density, including massive memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The absence of a GPU makes it less suitable for heavy graphics processing or large-scale LLM training, though its AMX instructions support efficient medium-sized LLM inference, processing 7B model prompts at 319.65 tokens per second. The hardware profile is optimized for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and complex data analytics.
